questions.q: What is Discovery, as a MID Server use case?
options: Scanning a customer's internal network to find and catalog configuration items, populating the CMDB
A way to open an inbound port into the customer's firewall
A feature that replaces the need for REST Messages entirely
A tool for writing Scripted REST APIs faster
questions.explain: Discovery uses the MID Server's presence inside the customer's network to probe and catalog CIs — servers, devices, applications — into the CMDB.

questions.q: Why can't ServiceNow's cloud instance run an Orchestration activity against an internal server directly, without a MID Server?
options: The instance has no network path to a system that lives inside the customer's own network, behind the firewall
Orchestration activities can only ever target cloud-hosted systems by definition
ServiceNow doesn't support running any kind of automation
Internal servers never accept any form of remote command
questions.explain: The MID Server sits inside the customer's network and already has a path to the target; the cloud instance does not.

questions.q: In the relay pattern, what actually changes when a REST Message or IntegrationHub action needs to reach an internal-only system?
options: Its connection & credential alias is pointed at a specific MID Server, so the real network call fires from inside the customer's network instead of from ServiceNow's cloud
The REST Message record and authentication profile have to be rebuilt from scratch
The integration must be rewritten as a Scripted REST API instead
Nothing changes; MID Servers only apply to Discovery, never to REST Messages
questions.explain: The integration is configured the same way as always — only the connection & credential routing points at a MID Server so the call originates inside the customer's network.

questions.q: Which three MID Server use cases does this lesson cover?
options: Discovery, Orchestration, and relaying REST Messages / IntegrationHub actions to internal-only systems
Billing, user provisioning, and license management
Email notifications, approvals, and SLA tracking
Report scheduling, dashboards, and performance analytics
questions.explain: Those are the three real, documented use cases this lesson grounds: internal network scanning, on-prem automation, and routing integration calls through the customer's own network.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say recognizing a MID Server need matters for the Chapter 8 capstone?
options: Because the fix for a firewalled target is a MID Server selection, not a redesign of the integration itself — exactly the kind of architectural judgment the capstone expects
Because every single integration in the capstone will require a MID Server
Because the capstone has nothing to do with network reachability at all
Because MID Servers are being deprecated before the capstone chapter
questions.explain: Not every capstone integration needs a MID Server, but knowing when one does — and that the fix is a routing change, not a rebuild — is the judgment call the capstone expects.
